newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish banks' short positions fell 30 pct in H1.
newsitem.headline: Turkish banks' short positions fell 30 pct in H1.

text.p: Turkish banks' short currency positions fell by 30 percent from end-1995 to $2.17 billion in the first six months of 1996, but this was up on the same 1995 period, a Treasury report said.
The report, on the Turkish banking sytem's financial structure and development, said banks' total currency positions were $3.09 billion at the end of 1995 and $2.03 billion in the first half of 1995.

"Although economic development encouraged banks to carry bigger short positions, economic and political uncertainties, lessons learnt from the 1994 (financial) crisis and new regulations caused them to reduce their currency positions," the report said.
Private banks led the way in carrying short currency positions with short positions totalling $2.07 billion in the first half of this year, down 7.5 percent from end-1995.
State banks' short positions in dollar terms dived 80 percent to $70 million and those of foreign banks shrank 65.6 percent to $152 million at end-June when compared to end-1995.
The report said development and investment banks had long currency positions worth $125 million after $52 million of short positions at end-1995.
